plotting_plan.title: Recorded Mean Squared Error for Three Intercept Corrections
plotting_plan.objective: Create a discrete scatter plot showing exactly the recorded pairs (b, MSE) = (0, 9), (1.5, 2.25), and (3, 0). Label the three observations and both axes. Present evidence only of the finite arithmetic on the same five observations used to compute the correction. Do not add interpolated curves, unmeasured points, uncertainty intervals, stochastic repetitions, or generalization claims.
plotting_plan.implementation_plan: Use R/ggplot2. Retain the editable .R source, vector PDF, and manuscript-compatible preview as downstream reproducibility artifacts. Include a caption stating that correction estimation and evaluation use the same five observations.

plotting_plan.title: Residual-Based Intercept Correction on Five Observations
plotting_plan.objective: Show the supplied computation: input x and target y; baseline prediction 2x; residual y-2x; mean residual b=3; corrected prediction 2x+b; evaluation on the same five observations. Draw explicit dependencies from x to the baseline, from y and the baseline to residuals, and from observed residuals to the scalar correction. Make reuse of the observations visible. Include no unrelated modules or experiments.
plotting_plan.implementation_plan: Use LaTeX/TikZ with mathematical labels and a compact layout suitable for the supplied single-column article. Retain the editable .tex source, vector PDF, and manuscript-compatible preview. Explain in the caption that the schematic describes the computation and supplies no evidence of predictive generalization.

introduction_strategy.candidate_paper_target: Inspect 10–20 macro-level candidates for the research graph; retain only directly relevant, verified citations for the short manuscript.
introduction_strategy.hook_hypothesis: Investigate whether foundational or survey literature supports using a simple residual correction calculation to explain systematic prediction offsets and the distinction between fitting and evaluation. Treat this as educational context, not evidence of real-world impact measured by this demonstration.
introduction_strategy.problem_gap_hypothesis: Frame the supplied problem as a finite instructional example: the fixed predictor 2x differs from y=2x+3 by a constant on exactly five observations. The note illustrates how the observed mean residual removes that offset on those same observations. Do not claim an unresolved scientific gap, a novel algorithm, benchmark superiority, or generalization.
search_directions: Find foundational or review literature on systematic prediction offsets and residual interpretation, using the query 'linear prediction residual interpretation systematic additive offset survey'. Use any discussion of practical consequences only as attributed context.
Find surveys or educational reviews using the query 'regression residual correction fitted error versus predictive evaluation review'. Exclude technical comparison papers reserved for Related Work.

Identify 3–5 foundational sources establishing the contextual concepts of linear prediction, residuals, and intercept estimation, using the query 'foundational linear prediction intercept mean residual estimation'. Verify identities rather than reconstructing papers from memory.

Find broad methodological references using the query 'same observations estimation evaluation limits predictive generalization review'. Connect these references only to the scope limitation explicitly stated in experimental_log.md.
introduction_strategy.citation_separation_rule: Reserve foundational and survey sources for Introduction. Assign each verified paper to one section only; do not repeat Introduction citations in Related Work.
introduction_strategy.evidence_boundary: Literature may contextualize the calculation but must not supply additional measurements, datasets, experiments, or claims of novelty. Search only material published on or before 2026-11.

subsections.limitation_hypothesis: For the exact observations in experimental_log.md, the fixed predictor 2x has residual 3 at every point because the supplied targets are 2x+3. This is a property of the constructed example, not an established failure of an external method.
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: Explain that the supplied calculation retains the fixed slope and adds the observed mean residual b=3, which exactly matches the five recorded targets. Present this as an arithmetic demonstration.

subsections.methodology_cluster: Mean-residual additive correction evaluated on its estimation observations
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Find technical papers through 2026-11 discussing mean-residual adjustments and evaluation when an adjustment is estimated from observed errors. Investigate distinctions between fitted error and predictive evidence without adding external methods as experimental competitors.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: The same five observations determine and evaluate b, so the recorded zero error does not establish performance on additional observations. The supplied correction does not resolve this evaluation limitation.
